title: First band in New Orleans and business back home
summary: He first played with Amos Riley around 1913; before moving he ran a pool room, soft-drink stand and boxing ring.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: When you, when you came down here, what was the first band you played with? You mentioned Jack Carey and, uh, Dooson, but was the first?
Well, uh, first band I called myself playing with was, uh, uh, Amos Riley. Oh, Amos Riley. Yeah.
Who else was in the band? Joe Howard. Joe Howard, yeah.

Yeah. Yeah, yeah. Well, I played with him with, uh, with the, with the first, you see, but he wasn't recommending it, uh, first to me, you see. What'd you, uh, be about, uh, uh, 15, did you say you moved here? Yeah, that, that, that was about, uh, uh, that was about the 15th, 1915. See?
During the First World War then? Yeah, yeah. The war had started. Yeah, yeah, yeah.
And, uh, if I'm not mistaken, I, I think I came on that in, in 1913. In 13. Yeah, yeah, yeah, yeah.

Yeah, yeah, yeah, yeah. 1913. Before the war. Yeah, before the war. Yeah, before the war. Because I, uh, Chris Gabriel, you see. Mm-hmm. And, uh, at least my wife came down, yeah. And I called myself coming down, yeah, not to wait. Yeah. I was in business up there. Well, the thing had got panty clothes on, you know?
Well, what kind of business did you have up there?

I had a pool room and a soft drink stand and beer and, uh, a boxing ring. Oh, all of that. Yeah, all of that, you see. Of course, we'd play music most every night, you see. Well, I just, every day was Sunday with us and a dollar at that time was a dollar. You know, you could, you could, you could so much out of a dollar, see. Yeah. On your own home and everything. Mm-hmm. People, you didn't have to spend your money. People made their own garden and raised their chicken and, like, yeah. People were living out there, you know. People on the plantation, well, they had no rent to pay. Yeah.

Of course, after they stopped moving in town off the plantation, you know, paying rent, and then working on the plantation, well, that kind of, it's just like today. That's all there. The thing is so high now, a dollar no, no value nothing. Yeah. No value nothing. See.
